lead.t: Pyogenic granulomas are pedunculated masses typically found on the gingiva of children, young adults, and pregnant women.

b: Benign , rapidly growing pedunculated/polypoid vascular lesion
Resembles exuberant granulation tissue histologically — NOT a true granuloma and NOT caused by infection (misnomer)
Common sites: gingiva, fingers, lips, oral mucosa
Associated with local trauma and pregnancy ( granuloma gravidarum )
Behaviour: can regress, fibrose, or mature into fibrous epulis/peripheral ossifying fibroma

b: Capillary hemangiomas presenting as rapidly growing red pedunculated lesions on skin, gingiva, or oral mucosa
Roughly a quarter follow trauma — reach 1–2 cm within weeks
Granuloma gravidarum — occurs in gingiva of ~1% of pregnant women; may regress after pregnancy or require excision
Treatment: curettage and cautery usually curative

qs.q: A pregnant woman presents with a rapidly growing, red, pedunculated lesion on her gingiva that bleeds easily. If this lesion is a pyogenic granuloma, what is the most likely treatment?
o: Radical excision of the underlying bone
Systemic antibiotic therapy for Bartonella henselae
Observation, as it will regress spontaneously by age 7
qs.e: Pyogenic granulomas are treated with curettage and cautery. They do not regress by age 7 (that is for juvenile hemangiomas) and are not caused by Bartonella in this context.
